key_insight: A filament oscillator model shows that coordinated ciliary waves can spontaneously switch between symplectic-like and diaplectic metachronal patterns, with stiffness controlling which state emerges.
engineering_relevance: The results inform how surface-bound active filaments should be tuned to maximize propulsion and control flow in synthetic microswimmers and bioinspired pumping systems.
method: Model each cilium with two degrees of freedom: phase along a prescribed beat sequence and overall orientation angle.
Simulate a spherical carpet of filamentous cilia to capture emergent coordination and propulsion simultaneously.
Sweep cilium stiffness and beat-plane tilt to test wave selection, swimming speed, flow structure, and rotation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical evaluation showing bistability at low stiffness, only diaplectic waves above a critical stiffness, and higher propulsive efficiency for diaplectic waves due to shorter wavelengths.
watch_item: The conclusions come from a model system on a sphere, so real ciliary carpets may differ in geometry, hydrodynamic coupling, and biological variability.
paper_title: Emergent coordination and propulsion of a model spherical ciliate
